method: Per azimuth bin (0 deg = north, eastward, 1 deg bins): march a ray from the site centre outward, bilinear-sampling the DEM, horizon elevation = max over samples of atan2(h_sample - h_observer - d^2/(2R), d), h_observer = centre height + 2 m eye height, R = 1737400 m (lunar curvature drop included). Local 10/20 m DEM inside 600 m, regional 30 m DEM (LDEM_75S_30M) beyond, out to 9990 m at the 13 south-pole sites; Apollo 15 is local-only. Terrain beyond the range is NOT in the horizon.
sources: LROC NAC DTM, Apollo 15 landing site (crop APOLLO15_E261N0036), via NASA Space ROS space-ros/simulation#32
rangeNote: Horizon from terrain within 9990 m of each south-pole site (600 m local DEM + 30 m regional DEM), 363 m at Apollo 15 (local grid corner). More distant massifs are not in the horizon; verdicts near the horizon can still differ from reality.
